title: ynh check --format json
description: Output of `ynh check --format json`. Runs every declared sensor and reports a gate verdict. Exit code 0 = pass, 1 = a blocking sensor failed, 2 = ynh could not run the check. Top-level oneOf accepts either the success payload or the cross-cutting error envelope.

Check.description: Check success payload. Emitted for both pass and blocked verdicts — a blocked gate is a successful run that found failures, not an execution error.

capabilities.description: Wire-protocol version. See CLAUDE.md capability-bump rule.

ynh_version.description: Binary release version or dev-build identifier.

harness.description: Name of the harness whose sensors were run.

verdict.description: blocked when at least one sensor with tolerance=blocking failed.

blocking.description: Failures that caused the verdict to be blocked. Always <= failed.

known.description: Sensors failing only in ways the baseline already records.

kind.description: Source variant of the sensor declaration.

tolerance.description: Effective tolerance — the default (blocking) is materialised here rather than omitted.

status.description: pass/fail/known apply only to command sensors. known = failing, but every failure is recorded in the baseline, so it is pre-existing debt rather than a regression and does not gate. reported = a files sensor surfaced content with no verdict derivable. deferred = a focus sensor needs an agent runtime ynh does not own. skipped = filtered out by --only. Only fail can gate.

new_count.description: Failures not present in the baseline. Set only for failing command sensors when a baseline exists.

known_count.description: Failures already present in the baseline.

new_output.description: Only the output lines absent from the baseline — what the author is actually being asked to fix.

BaselineInfo.description: Present when a baseline was loaded from .ynh/baseline/, or after --update-baseline wrote one. Absent when no baseline exists or --no-baseline was passed. One file per sensor, scoped by harness id.

recorded_at.description: When the oldest still-recorded sensor entry was accepted (RFC 3339). Oldest rather than newest: a ratchet is only as tight as its oldest forgiveness, and the entry nobody has revisited is the one most likely to be forgiving something already fixed.

known.description: Pre-existing failures forgiven across all sensors this run. Zero after --update-baseline, which reports what it recorded rather than comparing.

fixed.description: Baseline entries that no longer fail — debt paid off. Zero after --update-baseline, which reports what it recorded rather than comparing.

stale.description: True when fixed > 0: the baseline can be narrowed with --update-baseline. Zero after --update-baseline, which reports what it recorded rather than comparing.
